name: CO-STAR
description: Context, Objective, Style, Tone, Audience, Response. Suited to writing tasks where voice and audience matter.
source: GovTech Singapore's Data Science & AI team (https://www.tech.gov.sg/technews/mastering-the-art-of-prompt-engineering-with-empower/), made widely known by Sheila Teo's write-up of Singapore's GPT-4 prompt engineering competition (https://medium.com/towards-data-science/how-i-won-singapores-gpt-4-prompt-engineering-competition-34c195a93d41).

sections.label: Context
sections.helpText: Background the model needs to understand the situation. For example: "I maintain an open-source Python library for parsing CSV files, and I've just added streaming support for large files."

sections.label: Objective
sections.helpText: The task you want the model to carry out. For example: "Write a README section that explains how to use streaming."

sections.label: Style
sections.helpText: The writing style to follow, such as a particular expert, publication or genre. For example: "Follow the style of well-regarded project documentation, such as the Django docs."

sections.label: Tone
sections.helpText: The attitude of the response, such as formal, friendly or persuasive. For example: "Friendly and practical."

sections.label: Audience
sections.helpText: Who the response is for, so it's pitched at the right level. For example: "Python developers who already use the library but haven't worked with generators before."

sections.label: Response
sections.helpText: The format of the response, such as a list, a table, a report or JSON. For example: "A Markdown section with a heading, two short paragraphs and one runnable code example."

name: RISEN
description: Role, Instructions, Steps, End goal, Narrowing. Suited to multi-step tasks with a clear outcome.

sections.label: Role
sections.helpText: Who the model should act as, such as an expert in a particular field. For example: "You are a senior backend engineer with years of experience designing REST APIs."

sections.label: Instructions
sections.helpText: The core task, stated directly. For example: "Add cursor-based pagination to the GET /orders endpoint."

sections.label: Steps
sections.helpText: The steps to follow, in order. For example: "1. Read the current handler and its tests. 2. Propose a cursor format. 3. Implement it. 4. Add tests for the first, middle and last page."

sections.label: End goal
sections.helpText: The outcome you want, so the model knows what finished looks like. For example: "Clients can page through every order with no duplicates or gaps, even while new orders arrive."

sections.label: Narrowing
sections.helpText: Limits and requirements, such as length, scope, style or format. For example: "Keep existing response fields unchanged, add no new dependencies, and only touch the handler and its tests."

name: RACE
description: Role, Action, Context, Execution. Asks a reasoning model to work out its own approach rather than telling it.
source: RACE 2.0 by Trust Insights, which created RACE for AI prompting (https://www.trustinsights.ai/blog/2025/04/ai-prompting-frameworks/).

sections.label: Role
sections.helpText: Ask the model to choose a role for itself, and make sure the role contains superlatives. For example: "Which expert would handle this database migration best, and how would you describe that role using superlatives?"

sections.label: Action
sections.helpText: Ask the model to think about what it's doing and why. For example: "What needs to change in this code to fix the bug, and why does that change fix it?"

sections.label: Context
sections.helpText: Give the model a Deep Research report on the topic. For example: a report on the library you're upgrading, plus the relevant source files and the error output.

sections.label: Execution
sections.helpText: Ask the model to think through the outcomes and match it to the Action. For example: "For each approach you considered, what trade-offs does it make, and which one best fits the change?"

name: RTF
description: Role, Task, Format. The shortest framework, for quick requests.
source: No single verifiable origin. Role, Task, Format is the most common expansion; some sources use Request for the R.

sections.label: Role
sections.helpText: Who the model should act as. For example: "You are a senior backend engineer who specializes in SQL performance."

sections.label: Task
sections.helpText: What you want the model to do, stated clearly and specifically. For example: "Find out why this query is slow and rewrite it to use an index."

sections.label: Format
sections.helpText: How the output should be laid out, such as a list, a table or a short paragraph. For example: "Give the rewritten query in one code block, then a bullet list of what changed and why."
